subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: What would I like to be genuinely good at, and what will that cost me?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of setting a challenging but achievable personal goal in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe the technical and physical demands the goal implies using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply building the preparation the goal requires in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving managing setbacks, illness, and interruption; correct it and explain why.
Connect attempting the goal and evaluating the attempt with deciding whether to continue, adjust, or change direction and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Set, prepare for, and attempt one significant personal movement challenge chosen by the learner, then evaluate both the attempt and the preparation that led to it.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: The challenge is defined entirely by the learner relative to their own current capability; any goal that is meaningful and safe for that learner qualifies.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
